title: The Mud Towers That Outran Every Horse — Silk Road EP7 | China Travel Expert
description:
A chain of mud towers once carried news across the desert faster than any galloping horse. Would you walk this wall?

Along the Han-dynasty Great Wall near Dunhuang, a beacon tower stood roughly every 5 km — smoke raised by day, fire by night, each tower watched by a handful of soldiers under a Beacon Chief. A warning leapt from tower to tower down the line. A Han courier on horseback made about 300 li a day; the beacon relay was far quicker — later Tang rules even required the smoke signal to travel some 2,000 li in a day and night. Dunhuang's Han Wall still runs about 136 km, dotted with more than 80 rammed-earth towers.

🧭 Expert Tip: The best-preserved Han beacon towers sit west of Dunhuang near the Yumen Pass — pair them with the Mogao Caves for one desert-heritage day.
